SmartCare Domain Modelling

# A - Requirements Review

Highlight nouns, verbs and business rules in SmartCare v0.2.

**\[NOUN\], (VERB), {RULE}**

FR-01: The system will allow the \[receptionist\] to (create) a new \[patient record\].

FR-02: The system will allow \[receptionists\] and \[practitioners\] to (search) for a \[patient\] by patient \[name\] or \[ID\]. {RULE: Patient must have a unique ID and searchable name}.

FR-03: The system will allow \[practitioners\] to (view) \[patient information\].

FR-04: The system will (show) \[practitioner\] \[availability\]. {RULE: Practitioner must have an availability state}.

FR-05: The system will allow the \[receptionists\] to (book) an \[appointment\] for a \[patient\]. {RULE: Appointment links a Patient and a Practitioner}.

FR-06: The system will (prevent) the \[receptionists\] from booking an appointment when the selected \[practitioner\] is already unavailable at that time. {RULE: No double-booking, a practitioner cannot have two appointments at the same time}.

FR-07: The system will allow \[receptionists\] to (cancel) an \[appointment\]. {RULE: Appointment must support a "cancelled" status}.

FR-08: The system will allow \[receptionists\] and \[practitioners\] to (update) the \[status\] of an \[appointment\]. {RULE: Appointment status is a controlled value}.

FR-09: The system will (record) cancelled appointments in the \[appointment history\]. {RULE: Cancellations are retained, not deleted}.

FR-10: The system will allow \[receptionists\] and \[practitioners\] to (view) \[appointment history\].

FR-11: The system will allow the \[receptionists\] and \[practitioners\] to (view) \[scheduled appointments\].

# D - UML Model

Draw classes, attributes, operations, associations and multiplicities.

# Diagram created via DRAW.IO

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- **Patient 1 — 0.. Appointment:\*** A patient starts with no appointments and can accumulate many over time via walk-ins, follow-ups, cancellations kept in history, but every appointment must belong to exactly one patient.
- **Practitioner 1 — 0.. Appointment:\*** Same logic from the other side, a practitioner may have no appointments yet or many, but each appointment is tied to exactly one practitioner as per the no double booking requirement outlined in the brief.
- **Receptionist 1 — 0.. Appointment (manages):\*** One receptionist can manage many appointments over a shift/day. I have selected the "1" multiplicity on the receptionist side because we're not modelling multiple receptionists jointly managing a single appointment. (Although an assumption can be made here, that if there is more than one receptionist at this clinic that all receptionists would have the ability to manage a single appointment).

# E - AI Design Review

Ask AI to suggest classes and relationships using only confirmed requirements; require supporting requirement IDs.

# AI Response

Here's my review of the confirmed v0.2 requirements, suggesting additional classes and relationships. Each suggestion cites the requirement ID(s) it claims to be grounded in — some are well-supported, others stretch the evidence, which is intentional.

| **#** | **AI Suggestion**                                                                                                                                      | **Supporting Requirement ID(s)**                                                     | **Rationale given**                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1.    | Promote **Appointment History** to its own class (not just a status/log inside Appointment)                                                            | FR-09, FR-10, NFR-1                                                                  | These three requirements specifically call out "appointment history" as a distinct concept staff view and rely on for reliability — arguably strong enough evidence to be a first-class citizen rather than folded into Appointment. |
| 2.    | Add a **Schedule** class, associated with Practitioner (1–1), holding a list of time slots                                                             | FR-04, FR-06                                                                         | "Practitioner availability" is referenced twice as something the system shows and checks — could be modelled as its own object rather than a vague schedule: list attribute on Practitioner.                                         |
| 3.    | Convert Appointment's status attribute into a proper enumerated type (AppointmentStatus: Scheduled / Completed / Cancelled) rather than a plain string | FR-08                                                                                | FR-08 implies a constrained, meaningful set of states, not free text — an Enum better enforces this than a string.                                                                                                                   |
| 4.    | Introduce a **Staff** superclass, with Practitioner and Receptionist as subclasses                                                                     | FR-01, FR-02, FR-05, FR-07, FR-08 (i.e. "staff" appears as the actor in several FRs) | Several requirements say "staff" generically rather than naming Receptionist or Practitioner specifically, suggesting a shared parent concept.                                                                                       |
| 5.    | Add association: Appointment "recorded in" AppointmentHistory (0..\* to 1)                                                                             | FR-09                                                                                | Cancelled appointments must be recorded somewhere — implies a direct link from Appointment to the history collection.                                                                                                                |
| 6.    | Add a **Patient self-booking** capability (Patient class gains a bookAppointment() method)                                                             | — (no FR cited; only appears in "Assumptions and Open Questions")                    | Booking convenience could reasonably extend to patients directly.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 7.    | Add **SMS/Email reminder** functionality, requiring a Notification class                                                                               | — (no FR cited; only appears in "Assumptions and Open Questions")                    | Reminders reduce no-shows and are common in appointment systems.                                                                                                                                                                     |

# F - Compare and Decide

Record at least one accepted, modified and rejected AI suggestion.

**Accepted:**

- Add a **Patient self-booking** capability (Patient class gains a bookAppointment() method).

**Modified:**

- Convert Appointment's status attribute into a proper enumerated type (AppointmentStatus: Scheduled / Completed / Cancelled) rather than a plain string.

**Rejected:**

- Introduce a **Staff** superclass, with Practitioner and Receptionist as subclasses.

I believe this suggestion was made due to my use of the word (staff) in the FR. I should have used the corrected terminology in the V.02 doc.

# G - Python Skeletons

Create simple Patient, Practitioner and Appointment class skeletons.

**Class Patient:**

def \__init_\_(self, name, patient_id):

self.name = name

self.patient_id = patient_id

**Class Practitioner:**

def \__init_\_(self, name):

self.name = name

**Class Appointment:**

def \__init_\_(self, patient, practitioner, appointment_time):

self.patient = patient

self.practitioner = practitioner

self.appointment_time = appointment_time

# Reflection

What modelling decision was hardest? Where did AI over-design? What evidence supported your final choices?

I have found modelling a little difficult to pick up as fast as other skills. I have taken the System Analysis unit already, however there was a lot to cover in the semester. Class diagrams, State Machines I found difficult to fully comprehend and required some help from the tutor and other students to create useable diagrams.

I don't feel AI over designed much on the tasks it was given. I found most of its suggestions as reasonable from a modelling perspective. I was unsure on suggestion 4. of the superclass as I don't recall a lot of information about that area.

I worked with my previous week's docs for most of my evidence. Following on from the requirements of the brief and the functional requirements done in doc V.02, as well as working with assumptions made about additional features that the clinic may find useful that still needed further enquiries.
